subject: Energy
title: Air Mass and Atmospheric Effects
description: A fast breakdown of Air Mass and Atmospheric Effects for builders.

hook.text: Sunlight weakens as it passes through the atmosphere—dust, water, and gases scatter and absorb photons.

buildup.text: Air Mass 1.5 (AM1.5) is the standard reference—sunlight passing through 1.5 atmospheres at a 48° angle.

discovery.text: At noon on a clear day near the equator, irradiance peaks at about 1,000 W/m²—this is the standard test condition.

twist.text: Clouds don't eliminate solar output—diffuse light still generates 10–25% of clear-sky power on overcast days.

climax.text: High altitude sites get more intense sun—thinner air means less scattering, boosting solar cell performance.

punchline.text: Atmosphere filters sunlight—but plenty still gets through.

quiz.question: What is the standard test irradiance for solar panels?
